rv.q: It's perhaps too little too late, but ultimately still a welcome foray into fresh, feelgood territory for Bhatti.
At the end of the second half, I totally reverse my negative comments at the beginning.
In exploring the relationships of the choir though, there is not enough flesh on the bones in Bhatti’s writing.
Gooey play about a plucky community choir gearing up for a TV performance is cloyingly familiar
This is a gorgeously affectionately wrought production. A warm and welcoming hug of a show.
For me, it was an unexpected delight and a thoroughly enjoyable night out.
